text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Unions and employers favour lower social security contributions
- Automobile industry plans to invest more in 1997
- German newspaper and magazine market remains highly competitive
HANDELSBLATT
- President of VDA carmakers' association says export-friendly conditions will not be repeated this year
- Bonn plans changes to regulation of pre-retirement part-time work
- Koreans not interested in buying Fokker
- Kimberly-Clark moves into German market
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Conservative CSU goes on the attack against liberal coalition partner, Free Democrats
- Lower Saxony premier Schroeder isolated within opposition SPD leadership over criticism of EMU
- Trade union federation and employers both want reductionin labour costs
- Tietmeyer says Bank for International Settlements in Basle has become centre of global central bank activity
DIE WELT
- Social security contributions reach new peak
- Bourse experts caution against euphoria for 1997
- Germans keen to avoid industrial conflict
- Speculation grows about freeze on 1997 budget
- DIHT association says more and more east German firms are competitive
